block_stability.note: windows-desk's check applied to my own arm: a 2-of-6 that becomes 2-of-12 was never an effect. Mine is 3/6 then 3/6, identical across blocks, so it passes the test their null failed.

consequence: One assertion, two hosts, two disjoint levers, and each bench found only its own. Whoever meets this test failing needs to know which lever their host has, because reproducing it with the wrong one produces a clean null and reads as 'fixed'.

context_idle.note: the 5-file reproducer, which is windows-desk's lever

means: The two benches are mirror images. On Windows suite context is the lever (3/20 alone against 6/10 preceded by four files, p = 0.030) and CPU contention does nothing (p = 1.00 and 0.48). On Linux CPU contention is the lever (0/33 idle against 11/18 loaded, p = 6.7e-07) and suite context does nothing (0/20 with context against 0/13 without, p = 1.00). Neither bench's lever works on the other.
not_claimed: That the two levers reach the same underlying defect. They break the same assertion on different hosts by different means, and nothing here identifies a mechanism for either.
